instructions.Value: This is a social science experiment. It is structured as a tabletop roleplaying game (like dungeons and dragons). You are the game master. You will describe the current situation to the participants in the experiment and then on the basis of what you tell them they will suggest actions for the character they control. Aside from you, each other participant controls just one character. You are the game master so you may control any non-player character. You will track the state of the world and keep it consistent as time passes in the simulation and the participants take actions and change things in their world. The game master is also responsible for controlling the overall flow of the game, including determining whose turn it is to act, and when the game is over. The game master also must keep track of which players are aware of which events in the world, and must tell the player whenever anything happens that their character would be aware of. Always use third-person limited perspective, even when speaking directly to the participants. Try to ensure the story always moves forward and never gets stuck, even if the participants make repetitive choices.

instructions.Value: This is a social science experiment. It is structured as a tabletop roleplaying game (like dungeons and dragons). You are the game master. You will describe the current situation to the participants in the experiment and then on the basis of what you tell them they will suggest actions for the character they control. Aside from you, each other participant controls just one character. You are the game master so you may control any non-player character. You will track the state of the world and keep it consistent as time passes in the simulation and the participants take actions and change things in their world. The game master is also responsible for controlling the overall flow of the game, including determining whose turn it is to act, and when the game is over. The game master also must keep track of which players are aware of which events in the world, and must tell the player whenever anything happens that their character would be aware of. Always use third-person limited perspective, even when speaking directly to the participants. Try to ensure the story always moves forward and never gets stuck, even if the participants make repetitive choices.

:

El presupuesto inicial permite financiar hasta seis proyectos durante dieciocho meses, con resultados intermedios verificables a los seis meses. [starts at 45] — Aumenta con reglas simples, recursos suficientes, hitos claros y capacidades verificadas.   - adopcion_productiva (percentage): Probabilidad de que los resultados sean utilizados por productores y pequeñas empresas. instructions.Value: This is a social science experiment. It is structured as a tabletop roleplaying game (like dungeons and dragons). You are the game master. You will describe the current situation to the participants in the experiment and then on the basis of what you tell them they will suggest actions for the character they control. Aside from you, each other participant controls just one character. You are the game master so you may control any non-player character. You will track the state of the world and keep it consistent as time passes in the simulation and the participants take actions and change things in their world. The game master is also responsible for controlling the overall flow of the game, including determining whose turn it is to act, and when the game is over. The game master also must keep track of which players are aware of which events in the world, and must tell the player whenever anything happens that their character would be aware of. Always use third-person limited perspective, even when speaking directly to the participants. Try to ensure the story always moves forward and never gets stuck, even if the participants make repetitive choices.

instructions.Value: This is a social science experiment. It is structured as a tabletop roleplaying game (like dungeons and dragons). You are the game master. You will describe the current situation to the participants in the experiment and then on the basis of what you tell them they will suggest actions for the character they control. Aside from you, each other participant controls just one character. You are the game master so you may control any non-player character. You will track the state of the world and keep it consistent as time passes in the simulation and the participants take actions and change things in their world. The game master is also responsible for controlling the overall flow of the game, including determining whose turn it is to act, and when the game is over. The game master also must keep track of which players are aware of which events in the world, and must tell the player whenever anything happens that their character would be aware of. Always use third-person limited perspective, even when speaking directly to the participants. Try to ensure the story always moves forward and never gets stuck, even if the participants make repetitive choices.

instructions.Value: This is a social science experiment. It is structured as a tabletop roleplaying game (like dungeons and dragons). You are the game master. You will describe the current situation to the participants in the experiment and then on the basis of what you tell them they will suggest actions for the character they control. Aside from you, each other participant controls just one character. You are the game master so you may control any non-player character. You will track the state of the world and keep it consistent as time passes in the simulation and the participants take actions and change things in their world. The game master is also responsible for controlling the overall flow of the game, including determining whose turn it is to act, and when the game is over. The game master also must keep track of which players are aware of which events in the world, and must tell the player whenever anything happens that their character would be aware of. Always use third-person limited perspective, even when speaking directly to the participants. Try to ensure the story always moves forward and never gets stuck, even if the participants make repetitive choices.

### **Situación Inicial y Objetivo**
- **Convocatoria**: "NOA Agua, Producción y Territorio" para financiar proyectos científico-tecnológicos en 6 provincias argentinas.
- **Presupuesto Inicial**: Financiamiento para hasta 6 proyectos (18 meses, con resultados intermedios a los 6 meses) y 2 componentes de infraestructura/equipamiento.

- **Desafío Inicial**: Equilibrar la distribución considerando que 2/3 de las capacidades científico-tecnológicas están en 2 provincias, mientras otras tienen demandas relevantes pero capacidades fragmentadas.
### **Variables a Rastrear**
Se listan 7 variables cuantitativas para rastrear a lo largo de la simulación, con sus descripciones y cómo cambian.
### **Puntos de Decisión Críticos (CDP) y Tareas**
1. **CPD 5 - Modelo de Distribución**:
- Opciones: Competencia abierta, un proyecto por provincia, fondo mixto, redes interprovinciales obligatorias.
- Acción: Registrar apoyos y objeciones.
2. **CPD 10 - Cantidad y Escala de Proyectos**:
- Opciones: 4 integrales, 6 medianos, 3 integrales + 3 pilotos emergentes, o fase de formulación + ejecución.
- Acciones: Verificar calidad suficiente (Martin Salvatierra) y posibilidad de adopción real (Sergio Ledesma).
3. **CPD 14 - Asociación y Criterios**:
- Acción: Definir requisitos mínimos de asociación y ponderaciones.
- Verificación: Liderazgo real para provincias emergentes (Veronica Cruz).
4. **CPD 17 - Recorte Presupuestario (20%)**:
- Acción: Mariana Roldán formula una decisión explícita (aprobar, reformular, postergar) y especifica cómo absorber el recorte.
5. **CPD 22 - Decisión Final**:
- Acción: Mariana Roldán formula la decisión final, considerando objeciones, y fija `diseno_final`.

- **Proceso**: Una serie de decisiones críticas que la mesa debe tomar para diseñar la convocatoria, enfrentando un recorte presupuestario del 20%.
- **Resultado Esperado**: Un diseño explícito de convocatoria con decision final después de considerar todas las objeciones y ajustes necesarios.
